scoring.summary: Percentage of applicable baseline controls and enhancements assessed as Satisfied. FedRAMP defines no numeric score; the percentage is a reporting measure only. Open risks are rated and tracked on the POA&M.

rules.summary: Each determination statement is found either satisfied (S) or other than satisfied (O); there is no partial finding.
rules.quote: Each determination statement executed by an assessor results in one of the following findings: satisfied (S) or other than satisfied (O).

rules.summary: A control is Satisfied only when every determination statement for it is satisfied; any statement found other than satisfied makes the control Other Than Satisfied.
rules.quote: A finding of "other than satisfied" indicates - for the portion of the control addressed by the determination statement - potential anomalies in the operation or implementation of the control that may need to be addressed by the organization.

rules.summary: If the assessor cannot obtain enough information to make a determination, the statement is found other than satisfied.
rules.quote: may also indicate that the assessor was unable to obtain sufficient information to make the determination called for in the determination statement

rules.summary: Legacy FedRAMP POA&M guidance: Critical and High risks remediated within 30 days of discovery, Moderate within 90 days and Low within 180 days.
rules.quote: FedRAMP requires Critical and High risks to be remediated within 30 days of discovery, Moderate risks within 90 days of discovery, and Low risks within 180 days of discovery.

rules.summary: A High risk that waits on a vendor fix must be mitigated to Moderate with compensating controls within 30 days, and the vendor checked at least once a month. Vendor dependencies are not deviation requests.
rules.quote: High-risk VDs must be mitigated to a Moderate level through compensating controls within thirty (30) days.

rules.summary: A High vulnerability cannot be accepted as an operational requirement; it must be remediated or mitigated.
rules.quote: FedRAMP will not approve an OR for a High vulnerability

rules.summary: FedRAMP will not list the offering as FedRAMP Certified on the Marketplace while any High risk is open.
rules.cite: FedRAMP Playbook, POA&M, Do's and Don'ts
rules.quote: FedRAMP will not issue a "FedRAMP Certified" designation on the FedRAMP Marketplace if there are open High risks.

rules.summary: The POA&M timeframes above come from FedRAMP legacy documentation (reference only since 24 June 2026). FedRAMP's Vulnerability Detection and Response rules are mandatory from 7 December 2026, with a grace period to 7 March 2027 under a corrective action plan, and set their own remediation timeframes; check the current FedRAMP rules for the offering.

glossary.definition: Federal Risk and Authorization Management Program, the U.S. government program that authorizes cloud services for federal use.
Cloud Service Provider: the company offering the cloud service being assessed.
Third Party Assessment Organization, an accredited assessor that tests the controls.
Authorizing Official: the agency official who accepts the risk and authorizes the service.
Plan of Action and Milestones: the documented plan for correcting open risks.
System Security Plan: the document that describes the system and how each control is implemented.
Security Assessment Report: the assessor's report of findings.
Vendor dependency: a risk that can only be fixed once a vendor releases a patch.
Operational requirement: a finding that cannot be remediated without breaking the system.
